newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-May 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SING TAO -- China and Britain had huge differences over the role of the Joint Liaison Group after the handover. The British insisted that the JLG would supervise how the Joint Declaration would be carried out while the Chinese believed that the JLG would only be a liaison body.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- To strengthen security, the 100,000 policemen and coastguards in Guangdong province would not be allowed days off for two months. Local authorities had also been instructed to ban any kinds of demonstrations and postpone reporting any problems which were not related to the handover.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng gave a speech on developing China's nuclear energy, stressing that China should make use of foreign capital, facilities and technology.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Head of the National People's Congress Qiao Shi said Beijing would not meddle in Hong Kong's international affairs and that China would strengthen the development of its democratic and legal institutions.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong took measures to ensure its trading system would not be overloaded by the debut of heavily oversubscribed red chip Beijing Enterprises.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST --A radical opening -up of Hong Kong's court system was expected, following recommendations by a top-level judiciary think-tank to give the public access to hearings previously held in secret.

-- China's central bank had indicated to brokerages and commercial banks it would close treasury bond repurchase activities on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges in a continuing squeeze on stock markets.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD --The top five most powerful men in China would lead the nation into the next millennium sending a message of stability out to the world. Their rankings in the hierarchy would remain unchanged.
-- China's financial sector was in disarray yesterday as market rumours abounded of dismissals and resignations by top stock exchange and company officials.
